edges.description: Loss of the more effective C4A isotype reduces complement-dependent clearance of immune complexes and apoptotic cells.
edges.target: Reduced Immune Complex and Apoptotic Debris Clearance

edges.description: Zero C4A gene copy number lowers total serum C4, which falls with C4 gene copy number.
Persistent apoptotic debris and immune complexes provide self-antigen that drives autoantibody formation.
edges.source: Reduced Immune Complex and Apoptotic Debris Clearance
edges.target: Breakdown of Self-Tolerance and Autoantibody Production

edges.description: Autoantibody production and immune-complex deposition produce the lupus phenotype.
edges.source: Breakdown of Self-Tolerance and Autoantibody Production

nodes.description: Zero C4A gene copy number removes functional C4A protein from plasma, while C4B remains. C4A and C4B differ by only a few residues but C4A reacts preferentially with amino groups on immune complexes, forming covalent amide bonds, so C4A is more effective than C4B at immune complex handling.

evidence.reference_title: Differences between C4A and C4B in the handling of immune complexes: the enhancement of CR1 binding is more important than the inhibition of immunoprecipitation.
evidence.snippet: In the CR1 binding assay C4A was markedly more effective than C4B in enhancing binding to CR1.

nodes.description: Impaired clearance of apoptotic cells and immune complexes is linked to a breakdown of B-cell tolerance and production of antinuclear autoantibodies. The mechanistic chain downstream of defective clearance is supported mainly by C4-knockout mice, which abolish total C4 rather than C4A alone, so its application to human C4A deficiency is indirect.
nodes.id: Breakdown of Self-Tolerance and Autoantibody Production

evidence.reference_title: Complement C4 inhibits systemic autoimmunity through a mechanism independent of complement receptors CR1 and CR2.
evidence.snippet: Here we report high titers of spontaneous antinuclear antibody (ANA) in C4(-/)- mice.

evidence.reference_title: Complement C4 maintains peripheral B-cell tolerance in a myeloid cell dependent manner.
evidence.snippet: Deficiency in complement component C4 led to a breakdown in the elimination of autoreactive B-cell clones at the transitional stage

evidence.reference_title: Effects of Complement C4 Gene Copy Number Variations, Size Dichotomy, and C4A Deficiency on Genetic Risk and Clinical Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in East Asian Populations.
evidence.snippet: The main cause for C4A-deficiency among Europeans is the presence of mono-S coding for C4B1 and the absence of a long C4A gene in haplotypes with HLA-DRB1*0301.

evidence.reference_title: Gene copy-number variation and associated polymorphisms of complement component C4 in human systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE): low copy number is a risk factor for and high copy number is a protective factor against SLE susceptibility in European Americans.
evidence.snippet: Of the patients, 26% had only one copy of the C4A gene (i.e., heterozygous C4A deficiency), compared with 18.2% of unrelated controls (OR=1.61; 95% CI 1.1-2.4; P=.022).

nodes.description: Serum C4 protein concentration falls with C4 gene copy number, so C4A-deficient individuals tend to have reduced total C4.

evidence.reference_title: Low copy numbers of complement C4 and homozygous deficiency of C4A may predispose to severe disease and earlier disease onset in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: C4 serum levels were strongly related to C4 gene copy numbers in patients, the mean concentration ranging from 0.110 g/l (two copies) to 0.256 g/l (five to six copies; p = 4.9 × 10-6).

nodes.description: Classical-pathway opsonisation (C4b, then C3b) tags immune complexes and apoptotic cells for CR1-mediated transport and phagocytic clearance. With less functional C4 this clearance is impaired, so immune complexes and apoptotic debris persist. Direct human measurement of this defect is mixed: one study tied reduced prevention of immune precipitation to low C4A, while a later study (PMID:15932521) found the defect independent of C4A null alleles.
nodes.id: Reduced Immune Complex and Apoptotic Debris Clearance

evidence.reference_title: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus are deficient in complement-dependent prevention of immune precipitation.
evidence.snippet: PIP was positively correlated with levels of C4 (P = 3 x 10(-5)) and in particular the C4A isotype (P = 9 x 10(-10)) whereas C4B was redundant.

evidence.reference_title: Defective prevention of immune precipitation in autoimmune diseases is independent of C4A*Q0.
evidence.snippet: These results show that the PIP defect cannot be explained by low levels of C4A alone

nodes.description: SLE and lupus-like disease are the dominant clinical association of C4A deficiency. Homozygous C4A deficiency is one of the strongest common genetic risk factors for SLE, though it is a risk state rather than a fully penetrant cause, and the risk is confounded by HLA linkage (see discussions).

evidence.reference_title: Low copy numbers of complement C4 and homozygous deficiency of C4A may predispose to severe disease and earlier disease onset in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: Homozygous deficiency of the C4A isotype was identified as the strongest risk factor for SLE (odds ratio (OR) = 5.329; p = 7.7 × 10-3) in the case-control comparison.

evidence.reference_title: Low copy numbers of complement C4 and homozygous deficiency of C4A may predispose to severe disease and earlier disease onset in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: Two copies of total C4 and homozygous deletion of C4A were associated with a disease course requiring cyclophosphamide therapy (OR = 4.044; p = 0.040 and OR = 5.798; p = 0.034, respectively).

evidence.reference_title: Effects of Complement C4 Gene Copy Number Variations, Size Dichotomy, and C4A Deficiency on Genetic Risk and Clinical Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in East Asian Populations.
evidence.snippet: Homozygous C4A deficiency was infrequent in East Asian subjects, but had an odds ratio (OR) of 12.4 (P = 0.0015) for SLE disease susceptibility.
